observations.text: SP, due to a coarse power technique that did not keep Overtake under control, did not preserve the fingertip position as No2 and allowed the observance angle to open past 55 degrees on the outside of the turns. The IP directed the corrections and took the controls to re-establish the briefed position. The A/C was returned to route formation before the next leg.

SP, due to failure to shed a secondary task when workload increased on the navigation leg, did not maintain the vertical separation and settled more than 10 feet below the leader's plane. The deviation was not recognized and the IP directed the recovery, flying part of the correction. The fingertip position was regained only after IP input.

SP preserved the fingertip position within the standards required for this stage; however, lateral separation twice reached 20 feet beyond the reference point and was restored only after the IP's verbal prompts. The corrections were recognized with delay but were applied in the correct sense, without IP intervention on the controls. Marginal performance for the Training Section - timeliness of the lateral corrections is expected to improve.

SP controlled the A/C in a smooth and solid way, without abrupt corrections, and preserved the fingertip position with lateral excursions of about 15 feet beyond the reference point and an observance angle near 40 degrees. The deviations were self-detected and corrected in a timely manner without the IP's intervention. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP preserved the position determined in the Techniques and Procedures Manual, using engine power properly and trimming the A/C continuously throughout the navigation legs. Lateral separation stayed within 8 feet of the reference point, vertical separation within 4 feet and the observance angle within 30 plus or minus 5 degrees. Corrections were accurate and prompt, with no IP intervention. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP flew the fingertip position as No2 on both sides of the leading A/C with negligible deviations, holding lateral separation within 3 feet of the reference point and vertical separation within 2 feet. Speed Brake was used on the Leader's command and whenever required to keep Overtake under control, without prompting. Control inputs were smooth and solid and the observance angle was held at 30 plus or minus 2 degrees. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP, due to abrupt lateral stick corrections on an untrimmed A/C, did not control the A/C in a smooth and solid way and allowed lateral separation to exceed 20 feet beyond the reference point with repeated overshoots toward the leader. The IP directed the corrections and took the controls to re-establish the fingertip position. The remaining legs were flown from a wider position.

SP, due to a perceptual error in judging closure and lateral separation against the sun, did not keep Overtake under control and closed inside the 10 feet minimum lateral separation on the left side. Speed Brake was not selected when required and the IP intervened on the controls to restore separation. The position was regained only with IP assistance.

SP, due to late and insufficient power application on the outside of the turns, did not preserve the fingertip position as No2 and allowed the observance angle to open to about 50 degrees. The corrections were applied only after the IP's verbal prompts and the position was regained with delay. No IP intervention on the controls was required.

SP, due to distraction by navigation log work during the turn to the next leg, did not preserve the vertical separation stated in the Specific criteria and settled 10 feet below the leader's plane. The deviation was recognized only after the IP's verbal prompt and was corrected with delay. Vertical position was thereafter held closer to the reference.

SP preserved the fingertip position within the standards required for this stage; however, lateral separation reached 15 feet beyond the reference point on three occasions during the turns. Each deviation was recognized and corrected in a timely manner without the IP's intervention. Marginal performance for the Training Section - a more anticipatory power technique is expected to reduce the excursions.

SP controlled the A/C in a smooth and solid way, without abrupt corrections, using engine power properly and trimming continuously on both sides of the leading A/C. Lateral separation was held within 8 feet of the reference point, vertical separation within 4 feet and the observance angle within 30 plus or minus 5 degrees. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP preserved the position determined in the Techniques and Procedures Manual with negligible deviations throughout the navigation route, holding lateral separation within 3 feet of the reference point and vertical separation within 2 feet. Speed Brake was used from both sides on the Leader's command and to keep Overtake under control without prompting. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP, due to an over-controlled response to the leader's bank changes, did not control the A/C in a smooth and solid way and allowed vertical separation to exceed 10 feet low with the observance angle beyond 55 degrees. The IP took the controls and repositioned the A/C to the fingertip position. Recovery to route formation was directed before the next turning point.

SP, due to failure to state unable when the leader's maneuver could not be safely matched from the right side, did not preserve the fingertip position and allowed lateral separation to exceed 20 feet beyond the reference point. The deviation was not called on the radio and the IP directed the rejoin, flying part of the correction. The position was re-established only with IP assistance.

SP, due to a trim technique that left continuous back pressure on the stick, did not preserve the vertical separation stated in the Specific criteria and stabilized about 6 feet high on the leader's plane. The position was corrected only after the IP's verbal prompts, with delayed recognition of the drift. No intervention on the controls was required.

SP, due to insufficient recent practice in close formation from the left side, did not hold the observance angle at the briefed reference and allowed it to open to about 50 degrees during the turns. Each correction followed an IP verbal prompt and was applied with delay. Speed Brake was selected only when directed by the IP.

SP, due to slightly late power reduction on the inside of the turns, did not keep Overtake fully under control and allowed lateral separation to reach 15 feet beyond the reference point. The deviations were recognized and corrected in a timely manner without the IP's intervention.

SP, due to workload distribution that left the SP flying and transmitting at the same time over the checkpoint, did not hold the vertical separation at the briefed reference and drifted about 5 feet high. The deviation was self-detected and corrected without the IP's intervention. Control inputs otherwise remained smooth and solid, without abrupt corrections.

SP preserved the fingertip position as No2 on both sides of the leading A/C, holding lateral separation within 9 feet of the reference point and vertical separation within 4 feet. The corrections were accurate and timely but required more control activity than expected, and the observance angle twice reached 35 degrees. Marginal performance for the Training Section - smoother power and stick technique is expected to consolidate the position.

SP preserved the position determined in the Techniques and Procedures Manual with negligible deviations throughout the route, holding lateral separation within 3 feet of the reference point, vertical separation within 2 feet and the observance angle at 30 plus or minus 2 degrees. Engine power was used properly, the A/C was trimmed continuously and Speed Brake was applied from both sides without prompting. Control of the A/C was smooth and solid, with no abrupt corrections at any point of the navigation. Above end of block MIF achieved.
